A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Shot-by-Shot research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original AD generation experiments, shot-scale classification, thread prediction, component ablations, repeated runs, and human-alignment analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds Stage II model comparisons, inference-time measurements, and an analysis of description content and shot scales.

M1.justification: The two-stage pipeline, temporal sampling, thread clustering, scale-dependent prompting, and action-score computation are unchanged. The main-text replacement of DINO with DINOv2 matches v1's existing implementation details. Additional Stage II backbones are experimental configurations, without a revised proposed procedure.

E1.justification: CMD-AD, TV-AD, MAD-Eval, Thread-Safe, MovieShots, and the human-alignment tasks are retained. The added 100-movie correlation analysis remains within movie AD and shot-scale coverage; no distinct benchmark, domain, or prediction task is introduced.

E2.justification: Table A1 adds Gemma3-12B and Qwen3-8B as Stage II comparison models alongside LLaMA3-8B. The new timing comparison in Table A4 includes AutoAD-Zero. The comparator sets in the existing main benchmark tables remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds Stage II model comparisons with Qwen2-VL-7B fixed, per-AD runtime measurement, and GPT-4o extraction of descriptive elements from 100 movies for shot-scale analysis. Existing benchmark splits, frame-sampling settings, and evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds targeted analyses of Stage II backbone sensitivity, runtime costs by pipeline component, and the association between descriptive factors and shot scales. These supplement the retained temporal-context, thread-injection, factor-selection, human-alignment, and failure-case analyses.

E5.justification: v1 Table A3 already contains five runs, means, and standard deviations. v2 explicitly states that these are independent runs of both stages using different random seeds. The numerical entries are unchanged; this clarifies the existing reporting without establishing additional runs.

E6.justification: New results include Gemma3-12B Stage II action scores of 30.6 on CMD-AD and 24.7 on TV-AD, runtime totals of 3.75 seconds for Ours versus 2.82 for AutoAD-Zero, and factor-scale distributions in Figure A1. Existing numerical entries are retained. Appendix B reverses the stated evaluator order for unchanged LLM-AD-Eval score pairs.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4, the action-score construction, and the piecewise shot-scale prompting rule are unchanged. The new factor-scale study supplies empirical evidence, without adding formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free AD generation, film grammar, action evaluation, assisted selection, and benchmark performance. The new introduction sentence about interactions implied by shot structure elaborates the existing cross-shot contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly interprets Stage II model choice as less influential than Stage I choice, attributes most runtime overhead to contextual-frame processing, and uses content-scale associations to support the prompting rationale. Existing hallucination and story-level-context limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The added analyses disclose component-level inference times, an average contextualized clip duration of 19.82 seconds, and GPT-4o-based extraction of elements from 100 movies. Core implementation settings, Algorithms 1–5, and access links are retained. Timing hardware and movie-selection details are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds LAEO-Net++ when positioning interactions inferred across shots relative to earlier interaction recognition. Gemma 3 and Qwen3 references accompany the new comparisons. The LLaMA 2 reference replaces the earlier VideoLLaMA 2 citation used for that evaluator; most other reference changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: Limited edits clarify multi-shot Stage I inputs, specify DINOv2 in the main text, update an affiliation and acknowledgements, and expand Appendix C with short analysis paragraphs. The main narrative, section organization, and most wording are retained.

P2.justification: Table A1 gains a separate Stage II comparison block, and v2 adds timing Table A4 and factor-scale Figure A1. Existing appendix tables and figures are retained with renumbering and reflow, including moving the human-alignment plot onto a separate page.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the paper through targeted evidence for Stage II model choice, an explicit runtime breakdown, and a descriptive check of the shot-scale prompting rationale (Table A1, Table A4, Figure A1). It also clarifies the existing five-run experiment. These improve validation and transparency while preserving the principal results. Missing timing hardware and 100-movie sampling details limit the strength and reproducibility of the additions.
